instance_description:
Setting: A 2026 consumer-life finance workspace for one renter in Madison, Wisconsin, covering ordinary household money administration outside employment or business use.
Scope: Recurring activities include rent and utilities tracking, grocery and transit budgeting, subscription reviews, bill-payment preparation, refund follow-ups, warranty records, insurance paperwork, and annual record organization.
Resources: Later Scenarios may populate empty SQLite tables, text workpads, and the Wallet with account-neutral facts, draft notes, receipts, reminders, and case summaries.
Exclusions: No investing, credit underwriting, tax filing advice, legal strategy, medical billing advocacy, business bookkeeping, or irreversible high-stakes financial decisions.
personal_description:
Identity: Mina Solenne Faraday is a 34-year-old public library youth-program coordinator who rents a one-bedroom apartment and manages her own consumer finances.
Responsibilities: She maintains a practical monthly spending plan, tracks household bills, compares routine services, saves purchase documentation, and follows up on consumer issues.
Authority: Mina can organize records, draft messages, plan payments, categorize expenses, request refunds, and prepare information for insurers or merchants.
Restrictions: She does not manage anyone else’s money, trade securities, provide professional advice, override bank security controls, or authorize payments without explicit Scenario instructions.
